home.title: Someone made a fake account pretending to be you.
home.sub: Shield gets your friends reporting it within minutes, preserves the evidence properly, and drafts your cybercrime complaint. Free, no signup, works on any phone.
home.honest: Shield cannot delete an account. No tool can — Instagram has no takedown API, and anyone promising otherwise is lying to you. What decides the outcome is how fast a real cluster of people reports the account, how well the official report is written, and whether you escalate properly. Shield does those three things.
home.step1: Four questions, under two minutes. You get a link.
home.step2: A short code in your bio or story proves the real account is yours. This is what stops Shield being used against innocent people.
home.step3: Friends tap once, follow four steps, and the counter goes up. Meanwhile your evidence pack and complaint drafts are ready to download.

fraud.title: Money is involved. Do this first.
fraud.sub: Your contacts are being asked to pay someone who is pretending to be you. That is a financial crime and it is time-sensitive.
fraud.callD: The national cybercrime helpline. If anyone has already paid, the first few hours decide whether the money can be frozen.
fraud.portalD: Report it officially. Shield drafts the complaint text for you on the next screen.
fraud.warnD: One message to your groups: "Someone is using my name to ask for money. Do not pay. Do not send anything."

verify.title: Confirm the account is yours
verify.sub: Your case link stays private until we know you're the person being impersonated. That's what stops this tool being pointed at innocent people. Two ways to do it — the second is instant when it works.
verify.how: Add this code to your bio, or post it in a story, on {handle}. Then tap the button below. You can remove it straight after.
verify.failed: We couldn't find the code on {handle} yet. Instagram can take a minute to update. Wait a moment and try again.
verify.manualD: Your evidence pack, complaint drafts and escalation guidance are all available without verification. Only the public case link — the part that mobilises other people — needs it.
verify.skip: Skip for now, open my dashboard
verify.indeterminate: Instagram didn't send us your profile text, so we couldn't check. This happens often and it does not mean you did anything wrong — it means the platform withheld the page from our server.
verify.requestReview: Ask a human to check instead
verify.reviewSent: Sent for review. Someone will check @{handle} and publish your case if it's genuine — usually within a few hours. Everything else on this page works right now.
verify.reviewPrimaryD: We look at @{handle} ourselves and publish your case, usually within a few hours. This always works.
verify.autoD: Put the code below in your bio on @{handle}, then tap check. Instagram often refuses to show profiles to our server, so this may not work — if it doesn't, use the option above. It is not your fault.

manage.title: Your case
manage.shareD: Send this to your friends, your class group, your work group. Volume and speed are what matter.
manage.keepSecret: Keep this page private — anyone with this link can manage your case.
manage.checkFirst: Read it before you send it. Anything in [SQUARE BRACKETS] is for you to fill in, and nothing here is legal advice.
manage.captureBlocked: The platform blocked our capture — that is expected and common. Your own screenshots are better evidence anyway; upload them below.

ncii.title: Shield is the wrong tool for this, and there are better ones.
ncii.sub: What you're describing is image-based abuse. It is a crime, it is not your fault, and there are services built specifically for it that can do something Shield cannot: get the image blocked across multiple platforms at once, without you ever sending it to anyone.
ncii.adult: If you were 18 or over in the images
ncii.adultD: Use StopNCII.org. It creates a fingerprint of the image on your own device and sends only that fingerprint — the image itself never leaves your phone. Participating platforms then block anything matching it. Available in Hindi.
ncii.minor: If you were under 18 in the images
ncii.minorD: Use NCMEC's Take It Down instead. Same principle, but built for under-18s because the law treats these images differently. Do not use StopNCII for this.
ncii.moneyD: Do not pay. Paying almost always increases the demands rather than ending them. Stop replying, keep the messages, and call 1930.
ncii.keep: Keep the evidence, send it to no one
ncii.keepD: Screenshot the account, the messages and the profile. Do not forward the images themselves to anyone, including police — they will tell you what they need. Shield deliberately does not accept image uploads on this path.
ncii.notFault: None of this is your fault, and sharing these images without your consent is a criminal offence in India regardless of how they were obtained.

dispute.title: Dispute this case
dispute.sub: If a case names your account wrongly, tell us here. Three disputes take a case offline automatically while it is reviewed — you do not have to wait for anyone.
dispute.reason: What is wrong with this case?
dispute.reasonHelp: Be specific. If the account named is yours and it is not impersonating anyone, say so plainly.
dispute.doneD: Thank you. This case has been flagged for review.
dispute.suspended: This case has now been taken offline pending review.

guide.title: Making yourself harder to impersonate
guide.sub: Twenty minutes now saves the week you would otherwise spend on what you have just been through.
guide.s1: Take the handles next to yours
guide.s1D: Impersonators rarely invent a name — they take yours and add a dot, an underscore, or the word 'official'. Register those variants yourself on Instagram and hold them empty. It costs nothing and removes the most convincing option an impersonator has.
guide.s2D: Instagram settings → Account → Sharing and reuse. This stops your genuine account being suggested on the fake one's profile, which is the mechanism that quietly lends it credibility.
guide.s3D: An impersonator needs your pictures. A private account removes the supply entirely. If yours must stay public, at least review what a stranger can save from your profile grid and your tagged photos.
guide.s4: Tell your people what you will never do
guide.s4D: Set the expectation before you need it: you will never ask for money over a chat app, and you will never ask for an OTP. Say it once in your groups. It makes every future impersonation attempt fail on arrival.
guide.s5D: Most impersonation starts as an attempted takeover. Use an authenticator app rather than SMS — SIM swaps are common in India and an SMS code protects you from very little.
guide.s6D: Screenshot your own profile occasionally. If someone copies it, a dated screenshot showing the same photos on your account first is useful evidence.

about.title: About Shield
about.mission: Shield exists because the gap between discovering a fake account and doing anything useful about it is filled with panic, bad advice, and people selling takedown services that cannot work.
about.free: There is no paid tier, no email wall and no account. Shield is not a business and will not become one. It is published by amansploit as a public safety tool.
about.honest: It cannot delete an account. There is no takedown API and no private channel. What it does is compress the three things that actually decide the outcome: how fast a cluster of real people reports the account, how well the official report is written, and whether the escalation ladder gets followed to the end.
about.verify: A link that mobilises strangers to mass-report an account is a weapon unless the person creating it can prove they are the one being impersonated. So a case stays dark until the real handle displays a one-time code. It costs a genuine victim sixty seconds; it stops the tool being pointed at innocent people.
about.privacy: The fake account details, your chosen display name, your evidence, and a counter. IP addresses are never stored — only a keyed hash used to stop double-counting. Contact details are encrypted. Everything is deleted 90 days after the case is created.
about.legal: The drafts and citations are an assistive starting point compiled from published law. They are not legal advice and no lawyer has reviewed them for your situation. Read anything before you send it.
